overlap.title: Who is the “captain of the host of the Lord” that Joshua meets by Jericho?
overlap.summary: By Jericho Joshua sees “a man” with a drawn sword who calls himself “captain of the host of the Lord”. Joshua falls on his face and is told to take off his shoe because the place is holy. The passage does not say who or what this figure is, and his command about the holy ground does not explicitly identify him.
overlap.reasoning: The figure is first called “a man”, then gives himself a title found in the KJV only in these two verses, and Joshua answers by falling on his face and calling him “my Lord”. Whether Joshua is meeting a human officer, an angel or God bears on what Joshua’s act is and on who speaks next: the three verses give no message from the captain beyond the command about the shoe, and the next words of instruction are introduced with “And the Lord said unto Joshua” after a verse about Jericho being shut up.
overlap.scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. Readings that have been proposed, none of which the passage states: that the captain is an angel who commands the heavenly armies; that he is the Lord appearing in the form of a man, so that Joshua 6:2 continues the same meeting, a reading that points to the words about holy ground said to Moses at Exodus 3:5; that he is Christ before his birth, a reading held by some Christian interpreters. Limits on each: the Hebrew verb the KJV renders “did worship” here is the verb it renders “bowed himself” at Genesis 23:7, where it is done to men, so the verb alone does not show that the one bowed to is God, and a shared verb does not settle context; Revelation 22:8–9 has an angel refuse worship, which is quoted as a text used in this debate and not as an answer about Joshua; the passage does not say that the speaker of 6:2 is the captain. Brenton’s Greek of 5:14 as quoted has no word for “Nay” and no clause for “and did worship”; that difference is noted and not examined here. Check made: a search of the packaged KJV for “captain of the host of the Lord” and “captain of the Lord's host” finds Joshua 5:14 and 5:15 only; a search for “prince of the host” finds Daniel 8:11, which was not examined; Joshua 5:13–6:2 was read in the KJV. That is a word search, not a reading of the whole Bible. These checked verses do not explicitly settle who the captain is. No H or G is proposed. The Hebrew quoted is the Westminster Leningrad Codex digital text. A digital named edition is not proof that every manuscript agrees; other Hebrew manuscripts were not examined. The Greek is Brenton’s printed edition of the Septuagint, an ancient Greek translation tradition of the Old Testament. It is not a critical apparatus and does not show that all Greek witnesses agree or which reading is original. English in square brackets is the researcher’s plain rendering, not a KJV quotation and not a lexicon entry. The Greek New Testament wording is Tischendorf’s eighth edition as served by bolls.life (TISCH), compared with the Textus Receptus text served there (TR); neither is a critical apparatus.
